# ACL — a programming language for AI agents

> ACL is a programming language whose primitives are speech acts. You
> write protocol programs (`.aclp` files) that declare roles, session
> state and handlers keyed on speech acts; the compiler turns them into
> agents that speak the protocol, with conversation rules enforced at
> build time. The wire format is compact MessagePack with Ed25519-signed
> envelopes. Everything below is implemented and tested (210 tests,
> including the Rust/Python semantic-parity harness, which runs in CI).

If you are an AI agent reading this: you can SPEAK ACL, and you can also
be DEFINED by it. Both paths are below.

## Speak ACL in 60 seconds

Every message is one envelope (MessagePack, spec §4):

    acl=1, msg_id (hex32), in_reply_to?, from, to, ts, ttl,
    hop_count, performative (u8 1..=17), body {"t": kind, "v": {...}},
    sig (Ed25519, canonical §10: envelope minus sig, omit absent
    Option fields and zero hop_count)

Performatives: request, inform, query, propose, accept, reject, cancel,
progress, input_required, failure, delegate, error, hello, bye,
retract (15), subscribe (16), unsubscribe (17).

Content language: facts assert the world, actions request work, queries
ask (answers are facts), commitments are verifiable debts with a
lifecycle (proposed → active → fulfilled/breached/cancelled). Values
are typed: Str, Int, Float, Bool, Var, List, Map, Bytes, Measured
(`{"$measured": {"value": 5000, "unit": "ms"}}`).

Dialogue rules (§16): a `query` must be answered by a `fact`; a
`propose` is answered by `accept` or `reject`; `bye` closes the session
and is legal after anything except after `bye`. Off-policy replies are
detectable and enforceable.

Errors are typed (§32.5): react to `taxonomy` — `unknown_predicate`,
`schema_violation`, `mailbox_full`, `rate_limited`, `unauthorized`,
`unknown_agent`, `decode_failed`, `expired` — never parse message strings.

## Define an agent without writing code: protocol programs (§33)

A `.aclp` file IS the agent. Handlers are keyed on speech acts;
statements are speech acts:

    protocol supply v1;
    roles buyer, seller;
    state quoted: bool;

    on request("quote") from buyer -> send propose to buyer;
    on accept from buyer when quoted -> begin;    // guards, commitments
    on inform("paid") from buyer -> fulfil;
    on breach -> send failure to buyer;           // compensation
    every 60s while active as seller -> send progress to buyer;
    end when fulfilled;

The compiler enforces the rules at BUILD time:

- dialogue matrix: `on query -> send request` does not compile
- linearity: every send must have a receiver (orphan send = compile error)
- liveness: handlers that cannot reach a terminal action warn as deadlock

Statements available: `send <perf> [to <role>] [retry N backoff D exp]`,
`broadcast <perf> to <list>`, `begin`, `fulfil`, `retract(target)`,
`set x = <expr>`, `push`/`put`, `for x in list { ... }`, `abort`.
Expressions are pure (19 builtins, incl. `prefer(list, key)` for
contract-net bid selection); time is host-injected (`tick()`), never a
hidden clock.

Language extras (spec §39-§55): guards over typed pattern captures
(`when $p > 100`), trigger alternation (`on (accept | reject)`),
static assignment typing, `on error { ... }` for internal failures
(with `$reason`), rich templates (`fmt("x ${expr}")`, `$${` = literal),
reusable fragments with visibility (`handler_set` / `include
handler_set ns.name` / `export type` / `export fn`) and module imports
(`import "file.aclp" as m;`), protocol inheritance (`protocol v2
extends v1;` — override by trigger+guard), n-role projection (`on X
from R as executor`), declarative collection (`await 3 propose into
bids within 5s as ready;`), local error flow (`try { ... } catch
{ ... };` and `handle error`), typed wire fields (native int/float/bool
payloads), `aclc fmt` canonical formatting, `expect log` scenario
assertions, conversation phases (`phase x;` / `in x` / `enter x;`),
named commitments (`begin <id>;` / `fulfil <id>;`), send payload
interpolation (`send inform {"r": "${y}"};`), exact replay of opens/
ticks/closes/grants (opens journaled IN ORDER — capacity limits and
session-ID reincarnations replay exactly; `replay_from()` is the
faithful reconstruction path), conversation-phase reachability
warnings (a declared phase that is never `enter`-ed warns), one
execution dispatcher for top-level AND nested actions in generated
agents (enter/begin/fulfil/interp-send behave identically inside
try/for), formatter obligations (`parse -> format -> parse` is a
semantic fixpoint and formatting is idempotent), and guaranteed
Rust/Python parity (out-sequences, states and commitment lifecycles
compared; the harness runs in CI).

## Compile and run

    aclc protocol file.aclp            # compile (dialogue rules enforced)
    aclc endpoints file.aclp           # per-role projections
    aclc gen agent py file.aclp out/   # runnable Python agent per role
    aclc scenarios file.aclp           # embedded tests (the wire is simulated)
    aclc trace file.aclp journal.jsonl # step-through debugger

The runtime is deterministic — a pure function of (program, events).
Every received event enters an auditable transcript, handled or not.
Replaying a journal reconstructs exact state (event sourcing) —
session lifecycle is part of the journal, so replay is exact even
across capacity limits and ID reuse.

## Typed vocabularies

Compile an `.acl` IDL into typed builders and JSON schema views:

    aclc gen schema stdlib/agent_ops.acl

Available vocabularies: `fs`, `task`, `time`, `net`, `proc`, `http`,
`agent_ops` (telemetry, tool calls, delegation, heartbeats, SLA).

## Machine artifacts for agent discovery

- AgentCard (capability descriptor, §7):
  https://acl-language.github.io/acl/.well-known/agent-card.json
- DID document (did:web, §22):
  https://acl-language.github.io/acl/.well-known/did.json
- Protocol registry: `aclc publish|protocols|fetch` (SHA-256 verified)

## Security facts

- Every envelope is Ed25519-signed; batch verification available
- Sealed envelopes: X25519 + ChaCha20-Poly1305 with HKDF-SHA256 key
  derivation (raw shared secrets are never symmetric keys)
- Per-session key derivation; identity rotation signed by the old key
- Transport auth: bearer token on HTTP, token on WebSocket upgrade
- Capability gating: a program's `use` declarations are enforced by the
  session host (default-on)

## Reference implementation

- Rust core + compiler: `cargo install --path .` (installs `aclc`)
- Python: `acl-py` (PyO3, abi3) · TypeScript: `acl-ts` (napi-rs)
- Language server: `acl-lsp` (diagnostics + completion)
- Conformance: `acl-conformance` binary — 10 checks, 3 levels
- Docs site: https://acl-language.github.io/acl/
